verdict.left_looks: A long single-storey shop/saloon-style block with a flat, two-tone (pale grey over light tan) cap that reads as a thin fascia and a slightly tilted roof edge. The walls are almost entirely near-black with a repeating rhythm of tall pale-framed glass panes separated by black pilasters. The base is a checkerboard of dark and light stone-looking blocks. A wooden door sits in the centre, and interior furniture (sofas, crates, barrels, plants) is visible through the glass. The front reads clean and symmetrical, with a black-and-glass facade dominating the street view.
verdict.right_looks: A low, wide single-storey building with a dark, almost black body and a heavy overhanging roof: a dark top band over a brown-and-tan brick-patterned soffit-like fascia that projects well past the walls. The base is a grey stone plinth with a raised terrace and stone steps. Dense green leafy bushes and hedges flank the front, with lanterns on posts, a small table and chairs, a few wooden planters, an orange accent panel, and a cobble-textured sign block. Mixed materials, some asymmetry (the L-shaped plinth wall and the terrace) and layered vegetation read as deliberate, lived-in character rather than damage. The side and back are plain, dark walls with a stone base.
verdict.why: The right build has a stronger silhouette (the projecting roof and layered fascia), a terrace with lanterns and greenery that gives it a sense of place, and varied material texture, while the left build is a flat, repetitive black-and-glass box with a checkerboard base that looks more like a generic shopfront.
